title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page opens §1, 'Résultats de fidélité', of the manuscript around 'La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois'. It sets up the dictionary that the later anabelian 'faithfulness / full faithfulness' statements will rest on.

(1) Setup. To every field K one attaches its étale topos B_K = Spec(K)_et. This is a profinite Galois topos: it is equivalent to BG for G a profinite group, namely the category of discrete sets with continuous G-action.

(2) Points and separable closures. Π_K denotes the groupoid of points of B_K, i.e. the fundamental groupoid of Spec K. A separable closure K̄ gives a fibre functor L ↦ Hom_K(L, K̄) on finite étale K-algebras, hence a point. Grothendieck states that Π_K is canonically anti-equivalent to the groupoid of separable closures of K.

(3) Automorphism groups. For a separable closure K̄, the group of K-automorphisms Gal(K̄/K), which he calls E_{K̄/K}, identifies with the automorphism group of the corresponding point. He immediately qualifies this: it may be better to say it identifies with the opposite group. His reason is a variance remark: separable closures vary like fibre functors, which is opposite to how points vary under SGA4 conventions.

(4) Reconstruction of the topos. B_K is recovered from Π_K as the topos of continuous local systems on the profinite groupoid. Equivalently, it is recovered from E_{K̄/K} as the topos of discrete sets with continuous E_{K̄/K}-action.

(5) Transition. The last line starts the functoriality: a field homomorphism K → K'. The next page continues with the morphism of topoi B_{K'} → B_K, the map of groupoids Π_{K'} → Π_K and the map of Galois groups. This prepares the 'fidélité' statements, i.e. how faithful the functor from fields to profinite groupoids/topoi is.

Overall, this is foundational bookkeeping in groupoid/topos language (SGA1/SGA4 style) for anabelian Galois theory.
errors: No mathematical error. The statement 'anti-équivalent' and the identification with the automorphism group 'or its opposite' depend on the convention for morphisms of points. Grothendieck himself flags the ambiguity. Since everything is a groupoid, equivalence and anti-equivalence differ only by g ↦ g^{-1}, so nothing substantive is at stake.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard foundational setup (SGA1/SGA4) restated in groupoid/topos language for the anabelian program. The only personal touch is the explicit fuss over variance (points vs fibre functors), which is minor.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'topos ({+pro+}fini) galoisien' — 'pro' is inserted above the line, so the reading is 'topos (profini) galoisien'.
The stray '$\hat{}$' after the title is a mark ('^' / caret) in the margin, not part of the mathematics.
'il vaut peut-être mieux de dire' — the manuscript likely reads 'mieux de dire' as transcribed (sic), or possibly 'mieux dire'.
